discussion_comments.comment_body: This fetches every remote head SHA before the user has confirmed anything. On repos with many branches that can download a lot of history just to list unpublished commits. Consider limiting it to the upstream/default branch or using local remote-tracking refs.

Leaving this as is. Peak memory is about the same as before: main also held every checkpoint blob as a string at once, since all the per-file `git show` calls ran concurrently under `Promise.all`, each with its own stdout buffer. The batch buffer is released right after parsing, and blobs over 50 MB are skipped before they're read. A streaming parser would add a state machine for a constant-factor saving, which doesn't seem worth the extra complexity here.

🟡 **performance** (medium)

In the shell-integration fallback path, `returnCurrentTerminalContents()` already calls `getLatestTerminalOutput()` internally (which awaits it and emits the fallback message). The new telemetry code immediately calls `getLatestTerminalOutput()` a second time, so the entire clipboard capture round-trip (`workbench.action.terminal.selectAll` + `copySelection` + `clearSelection` plus two clipboard read/write operations) runs twice. The same duplication was added in the no-shell-integration branch (line 229). Besides doubling the latency/side effects of every fallback, the message that is emitted to the model and the snapshot used for the success telemetry can diverge because they come from two independent captures.

**建议**: Make `returnCurrentTerminalContents` return the snapshot it already fetched (`const terminalSnapshot = await getLatestTerminalOutput()` inside it) and reuse that value for the telemetry call, or fetch the snapshot once at the call site and derive both the emitted fallback message and the success flag from that single value.

**证据**: `const terminalSnapshot = await getLatestTerminalOutput()`

Keeping 15s as a single default, on purpose. Telemetry from the timed-out desktop devices: where the daemon did start, ~95% had it running within 7s of the old 8s cutoff, so inside 15s of launch. The 15-25s tail is a few percent of an already small group, and those devices still recover on the next launch exactly as they do today. 25s would also push the desktop worst case (up to 7.5s of login-shell PATH resolution + the wait) past the Tauri shell's 30s endpoint request. The cold-start cause is shared by every client that spawns the Hub from a compiled binary, so a desktop-only value would leave the CLI on the old limit for the same reason.

+import { execFile } from "node:child_process"
+import { createHmac, randomBytes, randomUUID } from "node:crypto"
+import { resolve } from "node:path"
+import { setImmediate } from "node:timers/promises"
+import { promisify } from "node:util"
+import { type ClineCoreStartInput, captureGitSnapshot, type GitSnapshotProperties, type ITelemetryService } from "@cline/core"
+import type { AgentAfterModelContext, AgentRuntimeEvent, AgentRuntimeStateSnapshot } from "@cline/shared"
+import type { Disposable, Event, Uri } from "vscode"
+
+const execFileAsync = promisify(execFile)
+
+// Never exported or persisted. A telemetry recipient cannot test candidate paths.
+// ponytail: IDs rotate on host restart; persist the key only if cross-restart identity is needed.
+const workspaceIdKey = randomBytes(32)
+type GitSnapshot = GitSnapshotProperties["git"]
+type GitRuntimeContext = Pick<GitSnapshotProperties, "runId" | "iteration" | "agentId">
+
+// Unlike prompt metadata, telemetry must also exclude query credentials and local remotes.
+export function sanitizeGitRemote(remote: string): string | undefined {
+	// biome-ignore lint/suspicious/noControlCharactersInRegex: reject unsafe URL input before parsing
+	if (!remote || /[\s\\\x00-\x1f]/.test(remote) || /^[a-z]:/i.test(remote)) return undefined
+	try {
+		const scp = !remote.includes("://") && remote.match(/^(?:[^@/:]+@)?([^/:]+):([^:].*)$/)
+		const url = new URL(scp ? `ssh://${scp[1]}/${scp[2]}` : remote)
+		if (!["https:", "http:", "ssh:", "git:"].includes(url.protocol) || !url.hostname) return undefined
+		url.username = ""
+		url.password = ""
+		url.search = ""
+		url.hash = ""
+		return url.toString()
+	} catch {
+		return undefined
+	}
+}
+
+export async function readGitSnapshot(cwd: string): Promise<GitSnapshot> {
+	const git = async (args: string[]) =>
+		(
+			await execFileAsync("git", ["-c", "core.fsmonitor=false", ...args], {
+				cwd,
+				// ponytail: cap each read at 1s/1MiB; split HEAD from status if large repos need better coverage.
+				timeout: 1000,
+				maxBuffer: 1024 * 1024,
+				windowsHide: true,
+				env: { ...process.env, LC_ALL: "C", GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS: "0", GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: "0" },
+			})
+		).stdout
+	let status: string
+	try {
+		status = await git(["status", "--porcelain=v2", "--branch", "--untracked-files=normal"])

discussion_comments.comment_body:
I measured the outputs — this gives ~132bytes per changed file. That makes ~7900 changed files exceeding the 1MiB limit.

That + 1s timeout are expensive work that can go wrong resulting with `{ state: "unavailable" }` and dropping the cheap work. 

The cases for that are likely major refactors, repo-wide format changes or big branch changes — likely moments signigifcant for Git timeline and worth recroding. 

Could we just emit what we know in case when we reach these limits? We may need a new `{ state: "partial" }` for it.
